w10_T4_000856: A plant nursery measures its beds in metres rather than in centimetres, and it counts everything else one by one. Early on Saturday morning the nursery had 171 seed trays in the shed, but 126 of them were cracked and were thrown away. Each of the good trays holds 8 planting cells. In the afternoon every one of those cells was sown with 8 seeds. The greenhouse is 24 metres long. By the evening count, half of all the seeds sown that day had failed to come up. How many of the seeds sown that day came up?
w10_T4_000857: Elena knits far more quickly than her friend Bruno does. On Monday Elena had 28 balls of wool in her basket, and 3 of them were tangled beyond use and thrown out. A wool shop that was closing down then gave her 60 more balls. Bruno's craft group asked her to make up 9 identical parcels, each holding as many balls of wool as she was left with. Every one of the 7 branches of that craft group then ordered a complete set of those 9 parcels. A dozen knitting needles lay in the bottom of her basket. How many balls of wool did the 7 branches order in total?
w10_T4_000865: In the morning the school library's returns trolley held 13 books. Before break 77 books came back from the classrooms, and by lunchtime another 53 had been returned to the trolley. During the afternoon 56 books were taken off the trolley and reshelved. The librarian's desk has 5 drawers. Later the head teacher asked for 4 trolleys to be filled, each with the same number of books as this one held, and in the evening exactly half of all those books were loaded into the van for the book fair. How many books went into the van?
w10_T4_000866: Marcus's tiling firm counts its stock in single tiles rather than in whole boxes. He had 216 tiles in the van and found 9 more under the back seat. He divided the whole lot equally between the 5 jobs on his list, and one job's share is exactly what is needed to tile a single wall. Each house on the new estate has 9 such walls, every street holds 8 identical houses, and the estate has 4 identical streets. How many tiles will the whole estate need?
w10_T4_000873: Early on Monday morning Rosa and her business partner Kenji unpacked 5 boxes of candles, each box holding 202 candles, and Rosa always unpacks more quickly than Kenji does. By midday a hotel had collected 310 of the candles from the store. In the afternoon a customer returned 33 candles that had never been lit. The workshop van has 4 seats. That evening Kenji tripled the number of candles in the store by finishing two more identical production runs. Overnight orders took 1346 candles out of the store. How many candles were left in the store?
w10_T4_000879: Bramble Farm keeps a careful record of the hens in its main coop. The coop held 138 hens in January, and 63 of them were moved to a neighbour's farm in February. In March 33 chicks that had grown up joined the coop, and in April another 26 hens arrived. A further 16 hens were bought in May, while 46 were sold at the summer market. The farmer now plans to build 8 coops on the hillside, each holding exactly as many hens as the main coop holds today. Half of the farm's fields lie beyond the stream. How many hens will the 8 new coops hold in total?
w10_T4_000883: Yusuf and his cousin Amara sell second-hand comics together, and Yusuf owns more of them than Amara does. Yusuf's crate held 141 comics until Amara doubled the contents by adding an identical collection of her own. A car-boot seller threw in 23 more comics for free. At the fair 139 comics were sold from the crate. A school donated 58 comics to the pair that afternoon, and 22 comics were later found to be water-damaged and thrown out. How many comics are in the crate now?
w10_T4_000886: A marathon's first water station was set up with 227 paper cups on the table, and a volunteer added 4 more from her bag. The organisers then dropped off another 50 cups at that station. There are 4 identical stations on the course, each set up with the same number of cups as the first. The race is run over 6 laps of the same circuit, and every station is restocked to that level for each lap. The finish line is 300 metres past the last station. A steward found 50 extra cups in a store cupboard and added them to the day's supply, and at the end 2293 cups were returned unopened. How many cups were used during the race?
w10_T4_000892: On Monday morning Ines counted 133 bags of compost in the garden centre yard, and her colleague Dmitri wheeled in 64 more, though Ines shifts more bags in a day than Dmitri does. By lunchtime 170 bags had been sold to landscapers. In the afternoon head office arranged for each of its 7 regional yards to hold the same number of bags as this yard, and that became the whole regional stock. That evening 76 bags were loaded onto a lorry for a golf course. A late cancellation brought 40 bags back into the regional stock. How many bags of compost were in the regional stock at the end of the day?
w10_T4_000895: Sofia had 30 chilli plants growing on her allotment, but 27 of them were destroyed by a late frost. Each surviving plant produced 6 chillies in July. She used 14 of the chillies to make a batch of sauce. Every chilli she had left was planted again, and each of those new plants gave her 8 chillies at the end of the season. Her plot is 12 metres long and she waters it twice a week. She then gave 23 of the chillies to her neighbours. How many chillies does Sofia have now?
w10_T4_000899: A rail company runs commuter trains made up of 7 carriages, and each carriage has 215 seats. On a normal weekday morning the company sends 5 of these trains into the city. Last Tuesday 5350 of those morning seats were booked in advance. The company then decided to double the number of unbooked seats by laying on extra services of exactly the same kind. How many unbooked seats were available in the end?
w10_T4_000905: Ben keeps his whole stamp collection in one album, and he owns more stamps than his friend Aisha does. The album held 64 stamps in January. Aisha gave him 37 stamps for his birthday and he put them straight into the album. In the spring Ben traded 54 stamps away at the collectors' club. He is 12 years old. In the summer he bought 55 stamps at a fair and later sold 24 of them to a dealer. How many stamps are in Ben's album now?
w10_T4_000906: Nadia manages a paper mill store and orders more stock than her colleague Ravi ever does. She took in 9 pallets of paper, each holding 195 reams, and stacked them all in one store room. A large print job used 215 reams from that room. Ravi returned 44 reams his department had not needed, and a supplier sent 41 more as a goodwill gesture. The company now wants 7 store rooms, each stocked with exactly as many reams as Nadia's room holds. How many reams will the 7 store rooms hold altogether?
w10_T4_000909: On Monday morning Kwame and his sister Adjoa counted the hens in the first hen house: Kwame counted 98 of them and Adjoa found 15 more hiding in the yard, and Kwame always counts faster than Adjoa does. Over the following week each of those hens laid 8 eggs. The farm has 9 hen houses, every one holding exactly the same number of hens as the first. On Saturday evening all of the eggs were packed into cartons holding 3 eggs each. How many cartons did the farm fill?
w10_T4_000914: A soup kitchen keeps all of its tinned tomatoes on one long shelf. In the autumn a delivery filled the shelf with 9 crates, each holding 93 tins. Over the winter 611 tins were taken from the shelf and cooked. In the spring the supplier restocked the shelf so that it held 7 times as many tins as were left on it. A volunteer then found 33 tins at the back of a cupboard and put them on the same shelf. How many tins are on the shelf now?
w10_T4_000919: A concert hall has 176 seats in its ground-floor block, but 100 of them were removed to make room for a bigger stage. The venue has 7 blocks of that reduced size on each floor, 4 identical floors in the building, and the group owns 8 identical halls. The group's newest hall opened 3 years ago. For last weekend's tour 14158 of the group's seats were sold. The box office then took back 19 returned tickets and put those seats on sale again. How many of the group's seats are still available?
w10_T4_000921: Early on Saturday morning a scout troop packed 182 sandwiches for the hike, but 106 of them were left behind at the hall by mistake. At the first stop the sandwiches they had were shared equally among the 4 patrols, and one patrol kept its share in a cool bag. Before noon that patrol ate 9 of its sandwiches, and in the middle of the afternoon it ate 7 more. In the evening a parent arrived at the campsite with 25 sandwiches for that patrol. How many sandwiches does the patrol have now?
w10_T4_000924: A community centre ordered 8 boxes of paint pots, with 39 pots in every box. A local school donated 58 more pots, and 77 pots were found to be dried out and thrown away. The centre's main hall is 15 metres wide. A summer camp used 200 of the pots over the holidays. A dozen brushes hang by the sink. The council now wants each of the 8 centres in the borough to hold as many pots as this one has left. How many paint pots will the borough's centres hold in total?
w10_T4_000925: In the morning the first machine at a bottling plant filled a tray with 240 bottles, but half of every tray was rejected by the inspector. Each box on the line holds 4 trays of accepted bottles. By the afternoon the boxes were being stacked 3 to a pallet, and each lorry takes 7 pallets. That evening 8 lorries were loaded from the day's run. Overnight 62285 bottles were delivered to shops. How many of the day's bottles were still waiting at the depot in the morning?
w10_T4_000929: Lena works faster on the cannery floor than her brother Otto does. In one hour 147 tins come off each of the 8 conveyor belts on Lena's line. Those tins are shared equally between 3 carts, and Otto wheels the carts away one at a time. The labelling room gets through 6 cartloads of that size every hour, and it runs for a shift of 5 hours. At the end of the shift 77 tins left over from yesterday were labelled as well. How many tins were labelled in total?
w10_T4_000932: On Monday morning a school kitchen had 53 cartons of milk in the fridge, and a delivery before break added 66 more. At lunchtime the head cook arranged for 4 fridges to be stocked with the same number of cartons as this one, and all of those cartons were counted as the kitchen's stock. Half of the kitchen staff were away with flu that week. During the afternoon 150 cartons were handed out at sports day. In the evening a supplier dropped off 76 cartons, and a nearby nursery returned 39 cartons it had not needed. How many cartons of milk does the school kitchen have now?
w10_T4_000934: Priya and her flatmate Jonas record their shared kitty in whole dollars rather than in cents, and Priya usually spends more from it than Jonas does. The kitty held 146 dollars at the start of the month. Priya spent 125 dollars on a big shop and then 1 dollar on a newspaper. Jonas put 41 dollars in after payday and Priya added 55 dollars from a refund. Later Jonas found 3 dollars in his coat and dropped it in, and their landlord returned a 56 dollar overpayment to the kitty. How many dollars are in the kitty now?
w10_T4_000935: On Saturday morning the food bank counted 209 tins on its shelves. Before noon a school delivered 25 tins and a church group brought in 47 more. At lunchtime a supermarket matched the whole collection, doubling the number of tins in the store. In the afternoon a second supermarket did exactly the same, doubling the total again. That evening a neighbour dropped off 47 tins on her way home. How many tins does the food bank have now?
w10_T4_000938: A theatre keeps all of its spare lightbulbs in one cupboard, and the electrician logs how long they burn in hours rather than in minutes. The cupboard held 126 bulbs in September, and 13 of them were found to be broken and were binned. The theatre group then bought enough bulbs to fill 7 cupboards of that size and stored them all in the one cupboard. Over the autumn season 283 bulbs were fitted into the stage rig. Over the winter season another 295 bulbs were used. How many bulbs are in the cupboard now?
w10_T4_000939: The town swimming club keeps all of its members in one register. There were 174 members in January, and 53 people joined in February along with 10 more in early March. In April 110 members let their membership lapse. A dozen lifeguards work at the pool. Over the summer 8 people joined in June, 45 joined in July and 57 joined in August. The main pool is 25 metres long. How many members does the club have now?
